question: Does OpenClaw intend the configured AI provider interaction to be a health or fitness service that may receive these expressly consented HealthKit aggregates under Apple's current terms?
rationale: The patch can technically constrain the command, but maintainers must own the product framing, privacy-policy change, App Store declarations, acceptable providers and use cases, and release timing for sensitive health data.

options.title: Approve bounded health service
options.body: Accept the aggregate-only, off-by-default direction after both defects are fixed, privacy and App Store declarations are ready, and signed-device proof passes.

options.title: Defer pending compliance readiness
options.body: Keep the direction open but pause this PR until the service framing, privacy policy, App Store declarations, and device-proof setup are finalized.

options.title: Reject provider disclosure
options.body: Do not ship HealthKit aggregates to configured AI providers and close this PR together with the linked feature issue.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded health service
recommendation.body: Accept the aggregate-only, off-by-default direction after both defects are fixed, privacy and App Store declarations are ready, and signed-device proof passes.

likelyOwner.reason: His prior merged ownership spans node-command authorization, pairing behavior, iOS signing, and release tooling, making him the best available owner for this cross-cutting product and release choice.
